findings.canonical_reading: The text says the book is divided into eight sections but explicitly names seven elemental paths: water, trees, earth, sun, wind, fire and lightning.
findings.todo: Decide whether an eighth elemental path is missing, whether the Mage Tower is intended as the eighth path/section, or whether 'eight sections' should be corrected to seven.

findings.canonical_reading: Magnus is ten when his magic becomes public and is described only as a young adult when he begins the journey.
findings.todo: Define Magnus's exact age when he begins the journey if later chronology requires it.
Choose a canonical name if the setting is reused.

findings.canonical_reading: The Lich King beneath the Mage Tower has no personal name.
findings.todo: Name the Lich King only if useful for future canon.

findings.canonical_reading: Enderdragon functions as title/species descriptor; no personal name is given.
findings.todo: Decide whether Enderdragon is a unique proper title or whether the individual should receive a name.

findings.canonical_reading: Magic can draw or store energy from sunlight, heat, gemstones and other sources, but costs and limits are not consistently formalized.
findings.todo: Define energy costs, storage limits and replenishment rules if tighter magic mechanics are desired.

findings.canonical_reading: The story explains lightning primarily as friction between clouds generating static electricity.
findings.todo: Science-curator pass: revise the lightning explanation toward charge separation within storm clouds, collisions among ice particles/graupel, electric-field buildup and discharge, while preserving simple language.

findings.canonical_reading: Azeroth is another world connected to Elysia through a portal, but its wider cosmology and relationship to Elysia are undefined.
findings.todo: Define the cosmology and portal relationship only if Azeroth or inter-world travel is reused.
